title: Regional bandwidth-aware rollout canvas
content:
Purpose:
This is a working canvas for a rollout that needs to be mindful of regional bandwidth constraints (egress caps, cross-region peering latency, and burst billing). The goal: release feature X across three regions while keeping latency SLOs intact and avoiding sudden egress surges that spike cost or saturate carrier links.

High-level approach (one-sentence):
Slow, topology-aware ramp with staggered traffic windows, proactive cache priming, and automated fallback to local model variants when egress thresholds are reached.

Quick summary of key constraints:
- North America (NA): high capacity, but evening egress peak between 02:00-05:00 PT (batching heavy).
- Europe (EU): medium capacity; peering to model-hosting region causes +40ms median tail if model served from NA.
- APAC: limited egress budget on the Dedicated cluster; bursts incur large billing step.
- Customers in regulated EU region must avoid routing through NA for any PII-sensitive requests.

Rolling calendar (coarse):
- Day 0 (2026-11-08): Dry run in canary NA region (10% of internal traffic, internal teams only). Smoke tests, QA pass gate.
- Day 2 (2026-11-10): NA slow ramp to 25% (03:00-07:00 PT window), monitor egress, latency, and cost-per-1M-tokens.
- Day 4 (2026-11-12): EU canary (5% of EU traffic routed to new variant during low-peak local hours). Verify compliance routing.
- Day 7 (2026-11-15): APAC pilot (internal and partner customers only), strict egress throttle (burst token=2000/min).
- Day 10 (2026-11-18): Global scaling decision; if all gates green, proceed to 75% NA / 50% EU / 40% APAC with staggered windows.
- Day 14 (2026-11-22): Full open (post-Thanksgiving window for NA avoided; if we hit costs we can pause).

Gating signals (pass/fail thresholds):
- Latency: 95th percentile must remain <= baseline + 25ms for each region during ramp window.
- Error rate: increase <= 0.2 percentage points vs baseline (any higher -> rollback).
- Egress burn rate: projected daily egress must not exceed defined budget by >10% over a 4-hour rolling average.
- Quality check: sample prompt set (50 prompts / region) QPS alt-eval score must not degrade more than 1.5% relative to baseline.

Operational checklist (pre-rollout):
- [ ] Confirm region-specific KMS keys and routing rules (security).
- [ ] Update routing policy: implement bandwidth-aware router config with per-region burst caps.
- [ ] Add observability dashboards (per-route egress, model-variant token count, tail-latency heatmap).
- [ ] Create a temporary cost alarm (Slack + PagerDuty) for egress budget >80% projected.
- [ ] Pre-warm cache in each region using synthetic low-priority traffic to prime KV caches and prefix caches (schedule: 1h before ramp).
- [ ] Validate canary test harness; smoke scripts and integration tests updated in GH PR 1456.
- [ ] Legal sign-off for cross-region routing for non-PII requests (EU exception documented).
- [ ] Ops playbook updated with rollback triggers and one-click routing toggle.

Runbook: day-of actions (anchor for the conductor):
- T-minus 60m: confirm on-call roster; Slack channel #launch-lattice active; deployer and telemetry leads in voice.
- T-minus 30m: run cache-priming job (5m traffic at 5rps) to cold nodes; confirm KV hit-rate >70%.
- T-minus 15m: enable safe-mode routing: all traffic still routed to baseline but measuring routing decision latency.
- T=0: flip NA canary, mark event in release log, start 15m tight monitoring window.
- T+15m: Decision checkpoint 1 (green/yellow/red). If yellow, reduce traffic and extend observation window. If red, immediate rollback.
- T+4h: Move to slow-ramp if all gates green.

Fallbacks and automatic mitigations:
- Auto-fallback to smaller-quant model variant if egress rate > cap for >5m.
- If tail-latency exceeds threshold and error rate climbs, router shifts traffic to dedicated low-latency variant in the same region (preserves PII constraints).
- Circuit-breaker: global kill-switch (feature flag) to revert all routing to stable baseline.

Region-specific notes and heuristics (unique bits):
- NA: for PG and CA subregions, stagger windows by PST offset to avoid overlapping backbone peak. Use larger batch sizes (up to 32) during low-latency windows to amortize kernel overhead.
- EU: enforce strict no-crossing for regulated tenants; test with synthetic EU-PROD requests that include GDPR markers to assert routing.
- APAC: use sample-sampling to reduce egress (send 10% of heavy prompts to local cached variant, rest to baseline) until telemetrying shows stable tail.

Telemetry snapshots to collect (minimum):
- tokens-in/out per-region, token-type breakdown (prompt/response).
- 1/5/15m tail latency percentiles per model variant and per region.
- KV cache hit ratio and prefix reuse rate.
- Egress bytes per minute and projected daily cost.
- Prompt set quality diffs: automated eval job -> per-region report.

Draft release notes (to iterate; keep short and customer-facing):
- Feature: "Adaptive Regional Routing" (beta). Purpose: improve latency and cost by routing to regional model variants and applying bandwidth-aware pacing.
- What changes for users: Most customers will see lower latency for regionally hosted workloads; enterprise customers on Dedicated can opt into stricter egress caps.
- Known limitations: APAC pilot has conservative throughput and may experience reduced throughput for very large payloads until local caches warm. Regulated EU tenants will not be cross-routed.
- Rollout plan: gradual, region-by-region; no action required from customers.

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self):
- Confirm which billing account receives egress charges for trans-Pacific peering (finance).
- Should we expose per-customer egress budget controls in Console now or in the post-rollout product ticket? (product decision)
- QA: need an expanded prompt set for APAC languages (JP/KO/EN-AU). Assign: Nora.
- Investigate whether local quantized variant yields equivalent quality for our eval prompt set; create microbench PR against /optimize.

Post-rollout follow-ups (1w, 4w):
- 1w: cost/latency retrospective; capture delta vs projected egress.
- 4w: finalize prioritization for Console egress budget controls and document recommended configs for Dedicated customers.

Notes and meeting fragments (informal):
- "If APAC pumps, we should revert and run a smaller burst schedule instead of full thermal rollback" — Diego.
- "Need to watch carrier-level alarms not just our egress dashboards" — Maya.
- Quick link: GHPR 1456 includes smoke scripts and synthetic traffic harness.

Bottom line: this canvas is intentionally conservative on APAC and strict on EU routing. The plan trades throughput for predictable cost and SLO adherence in the first two weeks. If we get green signals and cost matches model, open to more aggressive batching and global windows in phase 2.

-- End of draft --
